Which Group Blocks Actually Have Respondents on This Sheet

Source: R/format_xlsx.R
ck_nonempty_blocks.Rd

A grouping variable's levels are fixed across the whole table, so a country with no interviews for the questions on one sheet still gets a full block of columns there - every cell empty, or #NUM! where the estimator divided nothing by nothing. Those blocks are dropped.

Usage

ck_nonempty_blocks(dat, rows, blocks, idx, sample_base = NULL)

Arguments

dat

The table.

rows

The sheet's row indices.

blocks

All statistic blocks.

idx

The block indices assigned to this sheet.

sample_base

Base name of the denominator column (e.g. "n_total"), or NULL.

Value

The subset of idx worth writing. If every block would go, idx is returned unchanged rather than producing a sheet with no columns.

Details

A block counts as having respondents when its denominator column holds a finite value above zero somewhere in the sheet's rows. With no count column to read, the fallback is whether any statistic in the block is finite at all; NaN and Inf are not, which is exactly the case being removed.

The Overall block is never dropped - it is the reference column, and dropping it would leave a sheet with nothing to compare against.
